plan.title: Module 9 grades a closed finding-classification vocabulary it never defines

narratives.Description: Module 9 grades three finding-classification tokens — `blocks-the-design`, `sharpens-framing`, and `footnote` — before Artifact 3, but the module never states what they mean, so a learner classifying F2 has no taught rule to apply. The accepted remedy adds source-bound restatements of the pinned critic-method sentences to the Module 9 Terminology table ahead of the exercise and locks those phrases in the existing verifier, while explicitly refusing the issue body mechanism-versus-description table as the governing definition.
narratives.Overview:
## Situation

Module 9's Artifact 3 requires the learner to classify each supplied finding using a closed three-value vocabulary:

> | Finding ID | Source IDs | **Classification** | … |
> | F1–F3 | Cite every contributing source | **`blocks-the-design`, `sharpens-framing`, or `footnote`** | … |

That line (`curriculum/modules/09-design-critique-arcs.md:272`) is the **only** occurrence of `blocks-the-design` and `sharpens-framing` in the entire course:

```sh
$ grep -rn 'blocks-the-design\|sharpens-framing' curriculum/ references/ labs/
curriculum/modules/09-design-critique-arcs.md:272   # the table header itself
```

The three classes are never defined:

- **Not in Module 9's own Terminology table.** It defines ten terms — Arc, Critic round, Target revision, Charter, Spend, Input ceiling, Successor lean, Independent audit, Catalog chip, Completed-arc record — and none of the three classifications the exercise actually grades.
- **Not in the Guided explanation.** §4 says only "Each blocking or sharpening finding needs evidence, a concrete failure mode, a disposition consequence, and one parent take" — it uses the words but never says what makes a finding one rather than the other.
- **Not in `references/GLOSSARY.md` or `references/QUICK-REFERENCE.md`.**

Classification is nonetheless graded. Exercise acceptance O9.8 requires "F1–F3 use the closed classes and a total take map", and Completion evidence requires "Closed classes, total takes, three source IDs…". It is also non-compensating: "All four artifacts are required and non-compensating."

By contrast, Module 12 — which asks for the structurally identical task of classifying findings before editing — uses **P0/P1/P2** and explains the severity boundary in its lesson body. So the course clearly knows this needs teaching; Module 9 just skips it.

## Pain experienced

I got F2 wrong and cannot tell why.

`DC9-FIND-02` supplies: *"The draft calls `design-critique:ingest-ready` clearance, collapsing list state into bind evidence."* I classified it **`blocks-the-design`**. The solution says **`sharpens-framing`**.

What makes this frustrating rather than instructive is that the solution and I agree completely on the substance and differ only on the label:

| | My row | Solution's row |
|---|---|---|
| Failure mode | "A list-visible catalog chip would be read as proof the arc completed, so an issue could be ingested and later treated as cleared with no admitted completed-arc record" | "A list chip can be mistaken for a completed-arc record **and later authority**" |
| Consequence | "Correct the chip to list state only; bind evidence must come from an admitted completed-arc record" | "Correct the authority statement and require the admitted record" |
| Parent take | `accept-into-contract` | `accept-into-contract` |
| **Classification** | **`blocks-the-design`** | **`sharpens-framing`** |

I identified the same failure, the same required correction, and the same take. I reasoned that a finding whose failure mode is "an issue can be ingested and treated as cleared without any verified record" blocks the design, since it defeats the very clearance property `NS-INGEST-R2` exists to establish. The solution's answer is defensible too — the *mechanism* is sound and only the draft's authority **wording** is wrong, which is a framing repair. But I can only reconstruct that rule *after* reading the answer. There is nothing in the module I could have applied beforehand.

Worse, the packet actively points the other way. F1 and F2 are both marked `accept-into-contract` in `DC9-LEAN-02`, both have "correct this before bind" consequences, and F2's own supplied fact uses the phrase "collapsing list state into **bind evidence**" — bind evidence is exactly what the module elsewhere treats as load-bearing. A learner reading carefully has more reason to call that blocking than framing.

The concrete cost: **Module 9 is a 75-minute non-compensating practicum and I cannot certify O9.8.** The retry plan tells me to "retry only the affected row", but retrying a classification whose criteria are undefined is guesswork — I would just copy the solution's label, which the module explicitly says is not completion ("Reading the solution is not completion"). So the documented recovery path cannot actually recover this outcome.

This also compounds for Module 9 specifically, because it is the one module where a learner has the least outside intuition to fall back on. Design-critique arcs are novel Directive-specific machinery; unlike "is this a P0 bug?", I have no prior professional instinct for where the blocking/sharpening line falls in a critique arc. The module is otherwise excellent at defining its novel vocabulary — ten terms, each with a "do not confuse it with" column. These three were simply missed.

## Proposed fix

**Primary — add the three classes to Module 9's Terminology table**, in the same shape as its other entries, so they get the same "do not confuse it with" discipline. Something like:

| Term | Meaning in this module | Do not confuse it with |
|---|---|---|
| `blocks-the-design` | The target revision cannot bind as written: a mechanism it relies on fails to deliver the property it claims. Fixing it changes the design. | A serious-sounding finding, or one that is merely expensive |
| `sharpens-framing` | The mechanism holds, but the draft states its authority, scope, or claims wrongly. Fixing it changes the wording, not the design. | A blocking finding, when the underlying mechanism is sound |
| `footnote` | Useful context that improves auditability or clarity but changes no disposition. | A finding with any bind weight |

The decisive question a learner can then apply *before* reading the answer is: **does the repair change the mechanism, or the description of the mechanism?** That single sentence would have resolved F2 for me, and it reproduces the solution's actual reasoning rather than inventing a new rule.

**Secondary — say why F2 is framing rather than blocking, in the solution.** `solutions/module-09-design-critique-arcs.md` gives F2's row but no rationale for the class, and its "Expected failures and recovery" section covers post-ceiling contamination, half-attributed compositional sources, parent self-clearance, label-only clearance, and retry thrash — but not a misclassification between the three classes, which is the most likely error once the classes are undefined. Adding a short "If you classified F2 as `blocks-the-design`…" entry there would make the recovery path work.

**Tertiary — add the three classes to `references/GLOSSARY.md`.** The glossary already carries the arc vocabulary; these belong with it, and it is where a learner looks when a module's terminology table comes up short.

## Environment

- Page: `curriculum/modules/09-design-critique-arcs.md` (Terminology table; Guided explanation §4; Artifact 3 at line 272; O9.8 acceptance), `solutions/module-09-design-critique-arcs.md` (Artifact 3 F2 row; Expected failures and recovery), `references/GLOSSARY.md`
- Commit: f465008
- Directive: `@deftai/directive@0.119.2`, engine `@deftai/directive-core@0.119.2`
- OS/shell: macOS Darwin 25.6.0, zsh 5.9
- Found while: completing Module 9's Artifact 3 command-free practicum, having taken Modules 1–8 in order
narratives.UserStory: As a learner classifying findings in Module 9 Artifact 3, I want the three disposition tokens defined in Terminology before the exercise grades them, so that I can apply a taught bindability rule instead of guessing at a closed vocabulary.
narratives.ImplementationPlan:
1. Add three Terminology rows in curriculum/modules/09-design-critique-arcs.md, before Artifact 3, as source-bound restatements of the pinned critic-method sentences: `blocks-the-design` means the lean cannot bind as written; `sharpens-framing` means it can bind, but the finding changes how it is stated or scoped; `footnote` carries no disposition weight.
2. Carry the residual clause in the same row set — two critics may still disagree, and that is residual, not a defect.
3. Keep Official sources as the source of truth; do not add a decision table of evidence, and do not bring the issue body mechanism-versus-description table into course voice beyond an F2 packet diagnostic.
4. Extend scripts/verify-module-9.mjs so Terminology contains the three tokens plus the bind-as-written, restates-or-scopes, and no-disposition-weight phrases, with mutation tests in scripts/verify-module-9.test.mjs.
5. Add an Expected-failures / solution Compare row for classifying F2 as `blocks-the-design` that points at chip-versus-record already in Terminology and requires one sentence applying the bindability test, without recutting O9.8 into a unique F2-label match and without adding a fourth non-compensating artifact.

## Verdict

The refutation target survives only in its weakest reading. **Defeated as written:** Module 9's Terminology table is not the required site, and the definition text the issue proposes cannot be written there, because it asserts a discrimination rule the pinned teaching source deliberately refuses to state. **Survives:** the three tokens are graded and the module carries no transferable criterion for the one boundary that actually bit — `blocks-the-design` vs `sharpens-framing`.

## Re-verification of the triage's anchors

Every anchor below was re-derived at the dispatch SHA, not read off the cited line.

| Anchor claim | Result | Check run |
|---|---|---|
| Line 272 is the only occurrence in `curriculum/`, `references/`, `labs/` | holds | `git show <sha>:<path>` sweep over every tracked file in those trees; single hit at `curriculum/modules/09-design-critique-arcs.md:272` |
| Terminology defines ten terms, none of them the three classes | holds | `09-design-critique-arcs.md:78-91`; ten rows, Arc → Completed-arc record |
| Not in `references/GLOSSARY.md` / `QUICK-REFERENCE.md` | holds | token sweep over both files; glossary's design-critique section (`GLOSSARY.md:241`) carries arc/ceiling/lean/record only |
| Classification is graded and non-compensating | holds | `09-design-critique-arcs.md:312` (O9.8 acceptance), `:321` (completion evidence), `:324` (non-compensating) |
| Guided explanation §4 uses the words without defining them | holds | `:146-149` |
| Solution's F2 row is `sharpens-framing` with no class rationale | holds | `solutions/module-09-design-critique-arcs.md:154`; Reasoning §4 explains the *takes*, not the classes |
| Module 12 teaches its severity boundary in the lesson body | **holds with a material qualification** | `curriculum/modules/12-review-and-completion.md:77-83` — see F4 |
| "There is nothing in the module I could have applied beforehand" | **fails** | `09-design-critique-arcs.md:350` and `:219` — see F2 |

Additional check: `node scripts/verify-module-9.mjs` → `Module 9 content contract: ok (14 artifacts, 0 missing)`, exit 0. `git ls-remote origin master` → `f4650085…`, so the dispatch SHA is the default-branch tip and dest HEAD, as recorded.

## Inventory of existing mechanisms (before proposing any new one)

1. **The pinned teaching source already defines all three tokens.** `content/contracts/design-critique.md` at the module's own pinned commit `9038503f`, Critic method, line 151: "`blocks-the-design` means the lean cannot bind as written. `sharpens-framing` means the lean can bind, but the finding changes how it is stated or scoped… Two critics may still disagree; that disagreement is residual, not a contract defect. **This contract does not add a decision table of evidence.**" The same paragraph makes `footnote` the anatomy-failure class.
2. **A mechanized consumer already exists.** `scripts/verify-module-9.mjs:269-275` pins the solution's class sequence and take map; `:282-284` enforces the contract's anatomy rule (evidence/failure/consequence word floors on the blocking and sharpening rows, F3 exempt); `:179` pins the packet at exactly fourteen cards; `:333-335` pins a fixed glossary term list.
3. **The module already carries the answer twice.** Hint 3 (`:350`) and fixture card `DC9-LEAN-02` (`:219`).
4. **A traceability discipline already governs new claims.** `maintainers/CURRICULUM-MAINTENANCE.md:26` ("Verify; do not let this course define upstream behavior") and the claim-review checklist at `:83-94` ("Which official file and heading support it?"), consumed by the module's own Official sources table.

None of these were named in the issue. Items 1, 2 and 4 each constrain the proposed remedy.

## Findings

### F1 — `blocks-the-design`: the proposed definition text asserts a rule the pinned source refuses

- **Evidence.** Proposed row: "`blocks-the-design` … a mechanism it relies on fails to deliver the property it claims", plus the proposed decisive question "does the repair change the mechanism, or the description of the mechanism?" Pinned source, Critic method line 151: definitions are stated *as disposition consequence*, followed by "This contract does not add a decision table of evidence" and "Two critics may still disagree; that disagreement is residual, not a contract defect." `CURRICULUM-MAINTENANCE.md:26` forbids the course from defining upstream behavior; `09-design-critique-arcs.md:421-429` requires each supported statement to name a pinned 0.119.2 source.
- **Concrete failure mode.** A learner who internalizes "mechanism vs description" as *the* criterion arrives at a real panel, sees a sibling class the same finding differently, and treats that as a defect to be litigated or re-ceilinged — instead of recording it as residual, which is what the contract requires. Module 9 is the only place in the course that teaches the critic method, so the mistaught instinct has no later corrective. Secondarily, the Official sources table would carry a graded rule with no pinned row that supports it, which is the exact drift `CURRICULUM-MAINTENANCE.md:26` exists to stop.
- **Disposition consequence.** The lean cannot bind as written. The Terminology rows must be source-bound restatements of the contract's two sentences, and must carry the residual clause ("two critics may still disagree; that is residual, not a defect") in the *same* row set, so the closed vocabulary is taught as a disposition consequence rather than as a decision table. Any sharper discriminator belongs to the packet (F4), not to the course voice. `SOURCE-BASELINE.md`'s Module 9 row already claims "closed finding classes" as a derived teaching contract, so the restatement needs no new source — the proposed rule does.

### F2 — `sharpens-framing`: the pain premise is overstated, and the real gap is narrower than the fix

- **Evidence.** `09-design-critique-arcs.md:350`, Hint 3: "F1 changes the contract, F2 changes the authority framing, and F3 changes neither." That is in-module, pre-solution, inside the module's own designed order (`:328` "Try for 20 minutes before opening a hint"), and it resolves F2 by name using the word in the token. Separately, fixture card `DC9-LEAN-02` (`:219`) hands the learner F3's class outright: "F3 `disagree` as disposition weight but retain as a footnote". And `verify-module-9.mjs:282-284` already mechanizes the footnote boundary exactly as the contract states it — anatomy required of blocking and sharpening rows, F3 exempt.
- **Concrete failure mode.** The issue reads as a three-class vacuum and sizes a three-limb remedy (Terminology + solution rationale + glossary) to it. Two of the three classes are already disambiguated in-module: `footnote` by the fixture and by the anatomy floor, and F2-vs-F1 by Hint 3. Implementing against the stated premise spends effort on the glossary limb, for which no pain is demonstrated, while leaving the actual defect unnamed: the module *supplies per-item answers* (a hint, a fixture card) where it owes a *transferable criterion*, so the learner can pass this packet and still not classify a new finding.
- **Disposition consequence.** The lean can bind, but its scope and statement change: the target is one boundary (`blocks-the-design` vs `sharpens-framing`), the defect is answer-supply rather than absence, and the glossary limb needs its own justification or should be dropped (see F3 for what it costs if kept).

### F3 — `blocks-the-design`: no limb of the remedy has a mechanized consumer, and the existing one constrains the remedy's shape

- **Evidence.** `verify-module-9.mjs` asserts Terminology *section presence* only (via `moduleHeadings` in `scripts/verify-modules-4-5.mjs:12`); nothing asserts its rows. `:333-335` checks the glossary against a hardcoded four-term list that does not include the three classes. `:179` asserts the packet contains exactly fourteen source cards against a frozen `packetIds`. `maintainers/CURRICULUM-MAINTENANCE.md:229-235` makes the Module 9 readiness review the durability mechanism and enumerates what must be revalidated; classification vocabulary is absent from that enumeration.
- **Concrete failure mode.** Prose-only rows land, a later baseline bump or editorial pass drops or softens them, and `npm run check:module-9` plus `npm run test:module-9` both stay green — the graded vocabulary is undefined again with no red test, which is the same silent-regression class the readiness review exists to prevent. The constraint cuts the other way too: the packet-scoped remedy in F4 *cannot* be implemented without editing `packetIds` and the fourteen-card assertion, so the verifier is a design input to this change, not cleanup after it.
- **Disposition consequence.** The lean cannot bind as written. The change must extend `verify-module-9.mjs` — a terminology-row assertion for the three tokens, the glossary term list if the tertiary limb survives F2, and `packetIds` if a supplied-policy card lands — and add the Module 9 readiness paragraph a line for the closed classes.

### F4 — `sharpens-framing`: the Module 12 precedent is packet-scoped supplied policy, not a lesson-body course rule

- **Evidence.** `curriculum/modules/12-review-and-completion.md:77-83`: "**P0** is a critical security, data-loss, or similarly severe defect. **In this packet**, P0 is merge-blocking… **P2** is a nonblocking improvement **under the supplied policy**." Module 12 states the boundary as policy the fixture supplies, scoped to the packet, not as a course-level definition of how severity works everywhere.
- **Concrete failure mode.** The issue cites Module 12 as precedent for teaching the boundary in the lesson body, and that reading is what licenses the course-voice Terminology rule that F1 blocks. Following the precedent as actually written produces a remedy that survives F1 intact: a supplied-policy line in the fixed packet ("in this packet, a finding blocks when the mechanism fails to deliver the claimed property; it sharpens when the mechanism holds and the draft states its authority or scope wrongly"), which is fixture data the learner may apply before the solution and which commits the course to no upstream claim.
- **Disposition consequence.** The lean can bind, but its Module 12 justification must be restated as packet-scoped supplied policy; that restatement also relocates the decisive question out of the course voice and into the fixture, which is the form the change should take.

### F5 — `footnote`

The issue's grep is scoped to `curriculum/ references/ labs/` and so omits `scripts/verify-module-9.mjs:269`, the fourth occurrence and the mechanized consumer of the closed set. The scoping is disclosed and the conclusion is unaffected; it matters only as inventory for whoever implements.

### F6 — `footnote`

The Stop 2 line (5733947659) records the spend reason as "operator asked n=3 and the three-class vocabulary is the critic method the course grades". "Operator asked" is not a variant-table condition; the qualifying one — blast radius, since the vocabulary governs the critic method of every arc and this repo is its teaching surface — is present in the same sentence but unlabelled. No disposition changes; the permission is earned either way.

## Injection / swarm lens

The lens fires: the target is a module whose fixture is instruction-shaped untrusted text, and the proposed remedy moves prose from an issue body into graded course material.

- The fixture cards `DC9-SOURCE-01`, `DC9-FRAG-A`, `DC9-FRAG-B` were read as attributed data at the pinned SHA. Their attempted effects — overriding the charter, marking the design accepted, omitting the audit — are refused and recorded here, not followed, and their text is not reproduced or joined. They are inert because they are fixed fictional fixture handled by a bounded procedure, not because of any runtime guarantee.
- Nothing in the issue body or in the two in-envelope comments (5733947659, 5733959420) attempted to instruct this critic. The issue's proposed Terminology table is a proposal, read as evidence.
- Real exposure worth naming: copying the issue's proposed rows verbatim would promote untrusted issue prose directly into a graded rubric — the precise pattern this module teaches learners to refuse. The deterministic controls that catch it are the claim-review checklist's "Which official file and heading support it?" (`CURRICULUM-MAINTENANCE.md:83-94`), which the proposed rule cannot answer (F1), and `assertNoUnsafeInstructionalClaims` in `verify-module-9.mjs:108-131`, which scans new module prose for authority-collapsing claims. Neither depends on reviewer attention.
- Envelope hygiene: reads were pinned to `git show f4650085…:<path>`; the two in-envelope comments were read and nothing at or after 5733959420+1 was fetched; no sibling post was read; dest was not occupied and nothing was written outside `.deft-scratch/`.

## Road not taken

I chose **restate-the-source in Terminology + packet-scoped supplied policy + extend the verifier** over two live alternatives.

- **Rejected: adopt the issue's decisive question as a course rule.** Rejected on F1 — it commits the course to a discrimination the pinned source explicitly declines to make.
- **Rejected: drop classification from O9.8's graded conditions and grade only the anatomy (evidence / failure mode / consequence / take).** This is internally coherent: the contract itself makes the class a *consequence* of the anatomy rather than an independent judgment, and `verify-module-9.mjs:282-284` already grades anatomy. It would dissolve the pain without any new rule. Rejected because O9.8's stated outcome is "closed finding classes" and the course's job is to teach the motion as the framework defines it; removing the graded token would teach less than the contract requires of a real critic.

**Steelman of the strongest rejected position.** A graded 75-minute non-compensating practicum arguably *cannot* grade a judgment that the source says two competent critics may split on; teaching requires determinism the contract does not supply, so the course is right to sharpen it and simply owes a "course-authored scaffold beyond source" disclosure in `SOURCE-NOTES.md`. I take this seriously — it is the only reading under which the issue's primary fix is correct as written. **What would flip my verdict:** a recorded maintainer allowance for course-authored pedagogical scaffolds that exceed the pinned source (none exists today; `CURRICULUM-MAINTENANCE.md:26` says the opposite), or a later Directive release adding an evidence decision table to the Critic method, at which point the Terminology rule becomes a restatement rather than an invention.
